old: He was beginning to feel for himself that
new: He himself was beginning to feel that
reason: Source: 'He began to feel himself that he was certainly forgetting things'. In modern English 'feel for himself' reads as 'pity himself'; 'He himself was beginning to feel' keeps the source sense.

old: all the pleasures of life are _nihil est_ -- nothing --
new: all the pleasures of life are nothing -- _nihil est_ --
reason: Source: 'all the attractions of life _nihil est_'. 'are _nihil est_' reads 'are is nothing'; putting the English first and the Latin as his flourish keeps the italic Latin and the gloss without the doubled verb.

old: (perhaps she saw that they were pretending) but she kept talking
new: (perhaps she saw that they were pretending), but she kept talking
reason: Source: '(she saw perhaps that they were pretending), but she still went on talking'. The comma before 'but' was lost when the dashes became parentheses.

old: what was good; could not decide whom to blame
new: what was good; they could not decide whom to blame
reason: The restored clause put a semicolon before a subjectless 'could not decide'. Source: 'they did not know whom to blame, whom to justify'.

old: turned off his path, and walked along it toward the Hay Market
new: turned off his path, and crossed the bridge toward the Hay Market
reason: 'walked along it' leaves unclear whether 'it' is the bridge or the path and what he actually did; 'crossed it' makes the route clear. [verifier-modified: Source: 'on reaching the bridge he stopped and turning out of his way along it went to the Hay Market'. The 'it' is the bridge. 'crossed it' would still leave 'it' pointing at 'his path', so name the bridge.]

A translator's footnote appears mid-scene as if it were narrative, and 'The translator's note read' sounds like an object in the story; it at least needs to be marked clearly as an editorial note (an editor may prefer to move it out of the reading text).

old: whom he had supported almost since he was thirteen
new: whom the student had supported almost since he was thirteen
reason: With Raskolnikov and the student both in the sentence, 'he' is ambiguous about who supported the father from age thirteen.

old: their mother overhearing her talk in her sleep
new: their mother overhearing Dounia talk in her sleep
reason: 'her' could be the mother or Dounia; naming Dounia shows who talked in her sleep.

old: he smiled strangely at his sister and Razumihin's passionate plans
new: he smiled strangely at the passionate plans of his sister and Razumihin
reason: Heard aloud, 'smiled strangely at his sister' first sounds complete, so the listener has to reparse the sentence.
'Burnous' is an obscure period garment; adding 'cloak' tells the listener what it is and keeps the word.
